subject: biology
source_note: Topic structure follows the AQA A-level Biology (7402) specification subject content. Unit and topic names are spec-accurate; connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.blurb: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, ATP and water

units.name: Cells
units.blurb: Structure, division, membranes and the immune system

units.name: Exchange & Transport
units.blurb: Surface area, gas exchange, digestion and mass transport

units.name: Genetic Information & Variation
units.blurb: DNA, protein synthesis, meiosis, diversity and taxonomy

units.name: Energy Transfers (A-level)
units.blurb: Photosynthesis, respiration, ecosystems and nutrient cycles

units.name: Organisms Respond (A-level)
units.blurb: Stimuli, nervous & muscular coordination and homeostasis

units.name: Control of Gene Expression (A-level)
units.blurb: Mutation, gene regulation, genomics and gene technology

topics.name: Transport Across Membranes

topics.name: Energy & Nutrient Cycles

topics.name: Skeletal Muscle Contraction

topics.name: Homeostasis

connections.why: Amino-acid monomers polymerise into the proteins that act as enzymes
Digestive enzymes hydrolyse large molecules for absorption
DNA structure underpins how genes store and express information
Membrane structure governs diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Meiosis is the specialised division generating genetic diversity
DNA is replicated before a cell divides
Photosynthesis stores the chemical energy respiration releases as ATP
ATP from respiration is the universal energy currency
Low SA:V ratios drive the evolution of mass-transport systems
Blood transport delivers the substances homeostasis regulates
Monoclonal antibodies and vaccines apply recombinant technology
Motor neurones stimulate skeletal muscle to contract
Nervous and hormonal control together maintain homeostasis
Meiotic variation is the basis of inheritance patterns
Allele frequencies in populations evolve under selection
Energy flow and nutrient cycling shape population dynamics
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that flows through ecosystems
Mutation supplies the new alleles selection acts on
Understanding transcription enables recombinant DNA technology
Evolutionary relationships define taxonomy and biodiversity
